description: Consecutive catalogue number from 1 to 144. The canonical_source_id identifies the physical object independently of this numbering.
Source designation; aliases refer to the same physical object.
Canonical identifier used to match objects across tables.
Population label in the source compilation.
Adopted spin frequency.
Distance retained from the compilation, where available. A blank is not a zero distance.
two_sided_estimate or upper_limit.
Original thermal classification: strict, conditional, upper_limit, or flux_ceiling; defined in README.md. These labels do not classify r-mode stability.
Redshifted effective surface temperature: central estimate for a two-sided result, or the adopted ceiling for an upper limit. A flux_ceiling value is derived from luminosity.
Lower endpoint of the surface-temperature interval. Blank for an upper limit.
Upper endpoint of a two-sided surface-temperature interval; equals the adopted ceiling for an upper limit.
Reference redshifted core-temperature coordinate used for the catalogue display; derived through the envelope and stellar-structure models.
Lower endpoint of the displayed core-temperature range, including envelope and stellar-structure assumptions. Blank for an upper limit.
Upper endpoint of the displayed core-temperature range, or the reference ceiling for an upper limit. This is not a universal observational confidence bound.
Temperature or luminosity input as recorded in the compilation; units are stated in the entry.
Statistical or systematic meaning of the source interval, where known. No common Gaussian error model is imposed.
Energy band in keV, or a description identifying a bolometric or atmosphere-temperature result.
Atmosphere model retained in the compilation, where explicitly recorded. The flux_ceiling conversion assumes uniform blackbody surface emission.
Basis of the adopted spin frequency. For catalogue periods, the dated table supplies the period coordinate.
BibTeX key for the adopted spin value or compilation.
BibTeX key for the temperature estimate, upper limit, or luminosity input.
Persistent literature URL or catalogue URL corresponding to spin_reference.
Persistent literature URL corresponding to thermal_reference.
Location of the source in the compilation or cited literature. Living-table line numbers refer to the stated snapshot.
Source-specific assumptions and qualifications relevant to the adopted thermal constraint.
